description: Mixed-source dashboard by design (FRE-1211): 1 Postgres panel (Error events by type, route_traces.error_type/error_class) + 2 Elasticsearch panels (CPU & memory over time, sensor_poll; State transitions, state_transition). The FRE-1207 audit found no Postgres table for host sensor metrics or orchestrator state transitions anywhere in this program's plan, so forcing those two panels onto Postgres would mean inventing a source that would render empty forever -- failing the 'verified against real data' gate far worse than an honest Elasticsearch panel. Only the error-events panel had a real typed Postgres column to move to; moving it also fixed BUG-1 (the old ES panel's Lucene query used lowercase and/or/not, which Grafana's parser doesn't recognize as boolean operators, so it silently rendered an unfiltered top-10 event list under an 'errors' title). time.from is now-90d: the binding constraint is route_traces.error_type, whose 20 all-time rows span 2026-06-07 to 2026-08-07 (about 2 months) -- a shorter window (e.g. the dashboard's old now-24h) reads empty despite real error signal existing. The two ES families (sensor_poll, state_transition) both comfortably fit inside the same 90d window (spanning 2026-07-14 to today, live). The former 4th panel (Consolidation activity) was deleted per FRE-1212's audit disposition -- 38 days stale and redundant with extraction_retry_health's Postgres rebuild.

panels.description: Count of route_traces.error_type events over time (Postgres), replacing the ES-sourced version's BUG-1 (FRE-1207 audit sec.4): the old panel's Lucene query used lowercase and/or/not, which Grafana's ES parser only recognizes as uppercase AND/OR/NOT -- the lowercase tokens fell through as bare search terms, so a query claiming to filter for errors/failures while excluding error_monitor_* housekeeping actually returned the unfiltered top-10 event types (task_started, perplexity_query_started, etc., none error-related). Moving to route_traces.error_type/error_class sidesteps this bug class entirely -- there is no Lucene string to get case-wrong. degraded_stages was inspected too (skill Step 0) and excluded from this query: all 536 route_traces rows carry an empty array, so it currently carries zero discriminating signal. Verified live: 20 of 536 route_traces rows ever carry a non-null error_type (spanning 2026-06-07 to 2026-08-07), split LLMServerError (12), LLMClientError (3), sub_agent_failed (3), AttachmentUnsupportedError (2). Errors are rare -- the dashboard's time.from must cover at least this ~2-month span or the panel reads empty despite real signal existing.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(created_at,$__interval), error_type, count(*) AS error_count FROM route_traces WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at) AND error_type IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, error_type ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Error events by type

panels.description: Average cpu_load / memory_used from ES sensor_poll (query: event_type: "sensor_poll"), rebuilt in the Grafana UI on Elasticsearch -- no Postgres table exists anywhere in this program's plan for host sensor metrics, so a PG rebuild would be inventing a source (audit disposition: rebuild-in-the-UI-on-ES). Confirmed the query does NOT repeat the prior committed panel's bug (OR'ing in system_metrics_snapshot, dead test-harness pollution with mismatched field names cpu_percent/memory_percent): this query filters to sensor_poll alone, and live search confirms zero system_metrics_snapshot docs currently exist in the index at all. Both fields are 0-100 scale (verified live: cpu_load min 0/max 100, memory_used min 40.2/max 96.5), hence unit Percent (0-100), not percentunit. Verified live over the dashboard's 90d window: avg CPU 4.48%, avg memory 78.5% (126,607 sensor_poll docs, spanning 2026-07-14 to today, live) -- system is healthy, consistent with the VPS's 8 vCPU / ~10GiB envelope.
panels.title: CPU & memory over time

panels.description: Count of orchestrator state_transition events over time, broken down by originating state (from_state), rebuilt in the Grafana UI on Elasticsearch -- no Postgres table tracks orchestrator state transitions anywhere in this program's plan, so a PG rebuild would be inventing a source (audit disposition: rebuild-in-the-UI-on-ES). This panel's underlying query (event_type: "state_transition", Terms on from_state then Date Histogram) was already correct in the prior committed version -- confirmed against live data, not just trusted: the 3 from_state buckets (llm_call, init, tool_execution) match the field the orchestrator actually emits, and the query genuinely filters to state_transition docs (no BUG-1-style lowercase-boolean defect, since this query carries no boolean operators at all). What was stale was the committed DESCRIPTION's counts, not the query: it claimed 13,772 total docs / last emitted 2026-07-01, but the family is alive today -- verified live: 1,471 docs over the dashboard's 90d window (2026-07-14 to today), from_state split llm_call (602), init (494), tool_execution (375). Orchestrator is transitioning states normally.
